question: If sec A = cosec B and both A and B are acute angles, then the value of A + B is:
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

⇒ sec A = cosec B

⇒ 1/cos A = 1/sin B ⇒ cos A = sin B

⇒ sin B = cos A = sin(90° − A)

⇒ B = 90° − A

⇒ A + B = 90°

**∴ Answer = 90°**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** sec A = cosec B

**Formula:** sec A = 1/cos A, cosec B = 1/sin B

 
 A B Complementary Angles 

⇒ sec A = cosec B

⇒ 1/cos A = 1/sin B

⇒ cos A = sin B

⇒ Using identity: sin B = cos(90° − B)

⇒ cos A = cos(90° − B)

⇒ A = 90° − B (since angles are acute)

⇒ A + B = 90°

**∴ Final Answer = 90°**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

**Reciprocal Identities:** sec A = 1/cos A, cosec A = 1/sin A

**Complementary Relation:** sin θ = cos(90° − θ)

**Acute Angle Property:** If cos x = cos y, then x = y (for acute angles)

**Key Result:** If sec A = cosec B, then A and B are complementary
